A zero trust deployment separates its architecture into a control plane and a data plane. Which TWO components operate in the control plane? (Choose TWO.)
Policy engine
Policy enforcement point
Policy administrator
Implicit trust zone
Subject and system requesting access

The policy engine decides whether access is granted and the policy administrator carries out that decision by configuring the path. The enforcement point and the implicit trust zone sit in the data plane.

A company formalizes a quarterly enterprise risk assessment process and a written change management policy approved by the board. Under the standard security control categories, these controls are BEST classified as which category?
Operational
Physical
Managerial
Technical

Managerial controls address risk management and governance through policies, assessments and oversight. Technical controls are implemented in systems, and operational controls are carried out day to day by people.

A security architect needs to detect unauthorized modification of critical operating system and application configuration files on production servers and alert the team when a file changes. Which control BEST meets this requirement?
Data loss prevention
File integrity monitoring
Application allow list
Full disk encryption

File integrity monitoring compares current file hashes with a trusted baseline and alerts on changes, which directly supports integrity. Encryption protects confidentiality and does not report modification of files.

An attacker records encrypted TLS traffic for years and later steals the web server's long-term private key, yet is unable to decrypt any of the recorded sessions. Which property of the key exchange explains this?
Certificate pinning
Key stretching
Perfect forward secrecy
Salting
Perfect forward secrecy uses ephemeral session keys that are not derivable from the long-term private key. Pinning and salting do not protect previously recorded sessions.

A laptop fleet must encrypt local drives so that the encryption key is released only when the machine boots with an unmodified firmware and boot chain, and the key cannot simply be moved to another device. Which component BEST provides this?
Smart card reader
Trusted Platform Module
Key management service in the cloud
Hardware security module in a rack-mounted appliance

A TPM is a chip bound to the individual machine that can seal keys to measured boot state. An HSM is a separate appliance designed to serve many applications and is not tied to a single laptop's boot integrity.
Which TWO statements about symmetric and asymmetric encryption are accurate? (Choose TWO.)
Asymmetric encryption is generally slower than symmetric encryption for bulk data
Asymmetric key pairs can be used to create digital signatures
AES is an asymmetric algorithm
Symmetric encryption removes the need to securely share a key
RSA uses one shared secret key for both parties

Asymmetric algorithms are computationally heavier, which is why they usually protect session keys, and the private key signs data. AES is symmetric, symmetric keys must be shared securely, and RSA uses a key pair.

A legacy payroll server cannot support multifactor authentication. The security team restricts access to it through a hardened jump host limited to three source IP addresses and enables detailed session logging. Which control type does this arrangement represent?
Corrective
Deterrent
Preventive
Compensating

A compensating control substitutes for a requirement that cannot be met directly, here MFA. Preventive describes the function of the controls, but the reason they were chosen is compensation for a gap.

A help desk technician authenticates to a ticketing system, opens a ticket and tries to view an executive's HR record, which the system denies. Weeks later an auditor reviews which technician queried that record. Which AAA functions were involved, in order of the denial and the audit review?
Authorization, then authentication
Authorization, then accounting
Authentication, then accounting
Accounting, then authorization
The denial is an authorization decision based on permissions, and the later review depends on accounting records of activity. Authentication only proves who the user is.
A certificate authority hierarchy is being designed. To BEST limit the damage if an intermediate CA is compromised and to protect the trust anchor, how should the root CA be handled?
Kept online so that it can issue certificates quickly
Shared across partner organizations for cross-signing
Replaced by a self-signed certificate on each web server
Kept offline and used only to sign intermediate CA certificates
Keeping the root offline greatly reduces exposure of the highest-trust key, and intermediates issue day-to-day certificates. An online root defeats the purpose of the hierarchy.

A security engineer selects a hashing algorithm for verifying software releases. The primary requirement is that it be computationally infeasible to find two different files that produce the same digest. Which property is the engineer evaluating?
Collision resistance
Forward secrecy
Key stretching
Reversibility
Collision resistance means two different inputs should not yield the same hash, which matters for integrity verification. Hashes are intentionally irreversible.
An organization uses one wildcard certificate (*.example.com) on dozens of servers to simplify management. What is the MOST significant security risk of this practice?
Browsers never trust wildcard certificates
Wildcard certificates cannot use strong key lengths
Compromise of the single private key affects every subdomain that uses it
Wildcard certificates cannot be revoked
Because one private key is shared across many hosts, theft from any one server lets an attacker impersonate all of them. Wildcard certificates can be revoked and are broadly trusted.

Finance staff receive a message that looks like it came from the CFO's domain, though the reply-to address differs slightly. It urgently requests a wire to a new supplier and asks for confidentiality. Which attack is this MOST likely?
Business email compromise
Watering hole attack
Whaling through a malicious attachment
Credential stuffing
Business email compromise impersonates an executive to authorize fraudulent payments. Whaling targets executives as victims, whereas here the executive is the impersonated party.

A caller with a spoofed internal phone number tells an employee that the bank has detected fraud on their corporate card, and asks the employee to read back the one-time code just sent to their phone. Which social engineering technique is this?
Tailgating
Vishing
Typosquatting
Smishing
Vishing uses voice calls to manipulate victims, here to obtain an MFA code. Smishing would use text messages as the delivery channel.

A widely used IT management product ships a signed update that installs a hidden backdoor on thousands of customer networks. Investigators find the vendor's build server was compromised. Which attack category BEST describes this?
Supply chain attack
Watering hole attack
Zero-day exploit against customers
Insider threat
The attackers compromised a trusted vendor to reach downstream customers. The customers were not individually targeted through a vulnerability in their own systems.

A vendor announces that a remote code execution flaw in its web application server is being exploited in the wild and that no patch will be available for two weeks. Which action is the BEST immediate mitigation?
Deploy a virtual patch on the WAF or IPS and restrict network exposure of the server
Increase the password length requirement
Disable all logging to improve performance
Wait for the patch and take no action
A virtual patch and reduced exposure compensate for the missing fix. Waiting leaves an actively exploited flaw open, and password changes do not affect a code execution flaw.

A user opens a Word document and a macro launches PowerShell, which downloads and runs a payload directly in memory. No new executable is written to disk, and traditional signature-based antivirus raises no alert. Which malware type is this?
Rootkit installed through a driver
Logic bomb
Fileless malware
Boot sector virus

Fileless malware runs in memory and abuses legitimate tools such as PowerShell, which evades file-based scanning. A rootkit would require persistence below the operating system, which is not described.
A tenant in a cloud environment runs code that breaks out of its virtual machine and gains control of the hypervisor, giving it access to other tenants' workloads. Which vulnerability type is this?
Sandbox evasion in a browser
Virtual machine escape
Side-loading
Container image tampering
A VM escape lets code in a guest interact with the host or hypervisor. The other terms do not describe breaking out of virtualization.
A development team is concerned that attackers will exploit a stack buffer overflow by jumping to predictable memory addresses. Which operating system protection BEST makes this more difficult?
Address space layout randomization
Mandatory access control labels
Data masking
Salting of memory pages
ASLR randomizes where code and data load in memory, so attackers cannot rely on fixed addresses. The other options do not address memory layout.

A bank customer is logged in to the online banking site and, in another tab, visits a malicious page that silently submits a funds transfer request using the customer's active session. Which TWO controls BEST mitigate this attack? (Choose TWO.)
Anti-forgery tokens on state-changing requests
SameSite cookie attribute
Output encoding of user-supplied text
Parameterized database queries
Salted password hashing

This is cross-site request forgery. Anti-forgery tokens and SameSite cookies stop cross-origin requests from riding on the session. Output encoding stops XSS and parameterized queries stop SQL injection.

Attackers use username and password pairs leaked from an unrelated retailer's breach to log in to the company's customer portal, making only one attempt per account from many IP addresses. Which control is MOST effective against this attack?
Longer session timeouts
Account lockout after five failed attempts
Multifactor authentication
Blocking a single IP address
This is credential stuffing, and MFA stops stolen passwords from being sufficient. Lockout is weak because each account sees only one attempt, and the attempts come from many IP addresses.

Users who type the correct bank domain are being sent to a fraudulent site. Analysis shows the company's recursive resolver cached a forged record for the bank. Which control BEST prevents this specific attack?
Stronger TLS cipher suites
DNSSEC validation
Reverse proxy caching
Disabling ICMP
This is DNS cache poisoning, and DNSSEC digitally signs DNS records so forged answers fail validation. TLS settings would not stop resolvers from caching a bad answer.

An employee connects a personal wireless router to a wall jack in a conference room to get better Wi-Fi coverage. The router has default credentials and bridges onto the corporate LAN. Which term BEST describes this device?
Bluejacking device
Evil twin
Captive portal
Rogue access point
A rogue access point is an unauthorized AP attached to the network. An evil twin impersonates a legitimate SSID to lure users, which is not what happened here.

A team has two open findings. Finding A is a CVSS 9.8 flaw on an isolated lab server with no sensitive data and no network path from outside. Finding B is a CVSS 7.5 flaw on an internet-facing payment server and is listed in a known-exploited vulnerabilities catalog. Which finding should be remediated FIRST?
Finding A, because its CVSS score is higher
Finding B, because of exposure, asset criticality and active exploitation
Both at the same time, ignoring context
Neither until the next quarterly scan
Effective prioritization weighs exploitability, exposure and asset value in addition to the base score. Finding B is reachable and actively exploited on a critical system.
A critical patch has just been deployed to a fleet of web servers that were flagged in the vulnerability management program. Which step should come NEXT in the lifecycle?
Reclassify the vulnerability as a false positive
Close the finding based on the change ticket alone
Remove the servers from the asset inventory
Rescan the servers to validate that the vulnerability is remediated
Validation through a rescan confirms the fix worked. A closed change ticket proves only that work was attempted.

A credentialed vulnerability scan reports a database server as fully patched. Two weeks later, penetration testers exploit an unpatched flaw on that server that the scanner never reported. How is the scanner's result BEST described?
False positive
True positive
True negative
False negative
The scanner failed to report a real vulnerability, which is a false negative. A false positive would be reporting a flaw that does not exist.

At the start of an engagement, a penetration tester reviews the target's job postings, WHOIS records, public code repositories and social media profiles without sending any packets to the target's systems. Which activity is this?
Privilege escalation
Passive reconnaissance
Persistence
Active reconnaissance
Passive reconnaissance gathers information from public sources without interacting with the target. Port scanning would be active reconnaissance.

After compromising a workstation in the user VLAN, a penetration tester configures it as a relay so that tools on the tester's own laptop can reach a segmented database subnet that is not routable from the internet. Which technique is this?
Pivoting
Privilege escalation
Reconnaissance
Cleanup
Pivoting uses a compromised host as a stepping stone to reach otherwise inaccessible networks. Privilege escalation would raise rights on a system and does not provide network reach.
Which TWO observations are the MOST likely indicators that a user account has been compromised? (Choose TWO.)
Successful logins from two countries within ten minutes
A routine monthly password expiration notice
Large outbound transfers to an unfamiliar cloud storage service at 3 a.m.
An approved software update installing on the user's laptop
A completed scheduled backup of the user's profile
Impossible travel and unusual large off-hours transfers to unknown destinations are classic indicators of compromise. The remaining items are normal operational events.
A kiosk in a hospital lobby should run only one approved application and must resist unknown executables introduced from USB drives. Which approach is BEST?
Daily full antivirus scans
Application block list of known malware
Disabling the screen saver
Application allow list
An allow list permits only approved software and blocks everything else, including unknown malware. A block list only stops what is already known.

An attacker phones an employee claiming to be an external auditor, citing real project names and a fabricated deadline, and asks for copies of recent access control lists. Which social engineering principle-based technique is being used?
Dumpster diving
Baiting
Pretexting
Shoulder surfing
Pretexting builds a believable false scenario to extract information. The other techniques involve observation, discarded material or physical lures.

An attacker captures a valid authentication message between a client and a server and retransmits it later to gain access without knowing the password. Which attack is this, and which design element BEST mitigates it?
Replay attack; nonces or timestamps
Pass-the-hash; salting
Downgrade attack; longer keys
Birthday attack; larger buffers
Resending a captured valid message is a replay attack, and unique nonces or timestamps make old messages invalid. The other pairings do not match.

A data center hosts hundreds of virtual machines on the same subnet. After a breach, the team wants to prevent a compromised VM from reaching other VMs, even those in the same subnet, with policies tied to each workload. Which approach BEST achieves this?
Microsegmentation
Port mirroring
Perimeter firewall rule updates only
Larger subnet masks
Microsegmentation enforces workload-level policy for east-west traffic. A perimeter firewall does not see traffic between VMs in the same subnet.
An organization wants to discover which unsanctioned SaaS applications employees use and also enforce data protection policies on the sanctioned ones. Which technology BEST fits?
Hardware security module
Cloud access security broker
Network tap
Web application firewall
A CASB sits between users and cloud services to provide visibility, DLP and access control. A WAF protects a specific web application from attacks.
A company uses a SaaS customer relationship management platform. Which of the following remains the customer's responsibility under the shared responsibility model?
Maintaining the application code base
Physical security of the data center
Managing user accounts, access rights and the classification of data entered
Patching the underlying hypervisor
In SaaS the provider operates the infrastructure and application, while the customer retains responsibility for identities, access and its data. The other items belong to the provider.

A security team is deciding whether to use containers or full virtual machines for hosting untrusted workloads from different customers. Which characteristic of containers is the MOST significant security concern?
Containers cannot be scanned for vulnerabilities
Containers must always run with a hypervisor per instance
Containers share the host operating system kernel, so a kernel exploit can affect others
Containers cannot use network segmentation
Containers share the host kernel, so isolation is weaker than with VMs that each run their own kernel. Containers can be scanned and segmented.

An operations team replaces servers with freshly built images rather than patching them in place, and never logs in to change running instances. What is the PRIMARY security benefit of this immutable infrastructure approach?
It removes the need for vulnerability scanning
It guarantees that no vulnerability exists in the image
It eliminates the need for change management
It reduces configuration drift and unauthorized changes
Replacing instances from a known-good image keeps configurations consistent and makes manual tampering short-lived. Images still need scanning and change control.
A trading platform must handle full load during normal operation and keep processing without any failover delay if a node fails. Which high availability design BEST meets this requirement?
Weekly backup to tape
Active-passive cluster
Active-active cluster
Cold standby server
In an active-active cluster all nodes serve traffic, so a failure causes no failover pause and the remaining nodes continue. An active-passive design requires failover.

After a ransomware incident that also encrypted network-attached backups, management wants backups that the attacker cannot alter or delete even with stolen administrator credentials. Which solution BEST achieves this?
More frequent incremental backups to the same share
Mapping the backup share to all administrators
Compressing the backup files
Immutable or offline backup copies

Immutable or air-gapped backups cannot be modified during their retention window, which protects against credential-based destruction. More copies on the same writable share would be encrypted as well.
Which TWO controls protect data while it is in transit? (Choose TWO.)
TLS 1.3 for web connections
IPsec tunnel between two sites
Full disk encryption on laptops
Tokenization of card numbers in a database
Transparent data encryption on a database file
TLS and IPsec encrypt data as it crosses the network. Full disk encryption and transparent data encryption protect data at rest, and tokenization replaces values stored in the database.
A company needs tamper-resistant, certified hardware that generates and stores code-signing keys and serves signing requests from many build servers over the network. Which solution BEST fits?
Software keystore on a shared file server
Trusted Platform Module in each build server
Hardware security module
Self-encrypting USB drive
An HSM is a dedicated, tamper-resistant device designed to protect keys and perform cryptographic operations for many clients. A TPM is bound to one machine.
Public-facing web, mail and DNS servers must be reachable from the internet, but a compromise of any of them must not provide direct access to the internal LAN. Which design BEST accomplishes this?
Putting them in the same VLAN as the domain controllers
Connecting them directly to the internet with no firewall
Placing them on the internal LAN with host firewalls
Placing them in a screened subnet between two firewalls
A screened subnet isolates exposed services and limits traffic into the internal network. Placing them on the LAN gives a compromised host direct access to internal systems.

A firewall must automatically permit reply traffic for connections that internal users initiated outward, while dropping unsolicited inbound packets, without writing a separate rule for each reply. Which firewall type does this?
Stateful firewall
Stateless packet filter
Hub-based repeater
Proxy auto-configuration server
A stateful firewall tracks connection state and allows packets that belong to an established session. A stateless filter evaluates each packet independently against static rules.
A team wants to monitor traffic for malicious activity with no risk of adding latency or causing an outage if the sensor fails, and it does not need to block traffic. Which deployment is BEST?
Reverse proxy in front of every server
Inline IPS configured to fail closed
Passive IDS connected to a network tap or SPAN port
Load balancer with session persistence
A passive sensor on a tap or SPAN port sees copies of traffic and is out of the data path, so its failure does not interrupt production. An inline IPS can block but adds risk.
A remote access VPN uses split tunneling so only traffic for corporate subnets traverses the tunnel. What is the MOST significant security drawback of this configuration?
Corporate traffic is not encrypted
Internet-bound traffic bypasses corporate inspection controls
The tunnel cannot reach corporate subnets
VPN client software cannot authenticate users
With split tunneling, web traffic goes directly to the internet and avoids the proxy, DLP and filtering controls. A compromised endpoint can also bridge the internet and the corporate network.

A business requires recovery of its operations within about 24 to 72 hours after a disaster. The recovery site should have hardware and connectivity already installed, with data restored from backups when needed, at a lower cost than a hot site. Which site type is BEST?
Warm site
Hot site
Cold site
Mobile command post only
A warm site has equipment and connectivity in place but needs data restoration, which balances cost and recovery time. A cold site would have little or no equipment, and a hot site is more expensive.

A company wants any device plugged into a switch port to remain unable to pass traffic, other than authentication traffic, until the device or its user is successfully authenticated. Which technology BEST meets this requirement?
802.1X port-based access control
Spanning tree protocol
Port mirroring
DHCP lease reduction
802.1X keeps the port in an unauthorized state until authentication succeeds with a RADIUS server. STP prevents loops and does not authenticate devices.

An industrial plant must send production metrics from the OT network to corporate reporting systems, but there must be no possible return path for traffic from the corporate network into OT. Which solution BEST meets this requirement?
Site-to-site VPN with split tunneling
Data diode or unidirectional gateway
Stateful firewall allowing established sessions
Wireless bridge between networks
A data diode enforces one-way data flow physically or logically. Stateful firewalls and VPNs allow two-way sessions that could be abused to reach OT systems.

A compliance team wants scanners to automatically check hundreds of servers against an approved hardening baseline, using standardized, machine-readable content and reporting results consistently. Which standard is designed for this?
SCAP
TAXII
SPF
CVSS
The Security Content Automation Protocol standardizes the expression and checking of configuration and vulnerability data. TAXII transports threat intelligence and CVSS scores severity.

The SOC wants to receive indicators of compromise from a partner automatically and in near real time. Which standard defines the transport mechanism for exchanging this threat intelligence over HTTPS?
STIX
TAXII
OVAL
CPE
TAXII is the transport protocol for sharing cyber threat intelligence, while STIX defines the language and format of the data.
Dark web monitoring shows that credentials for dozens of the company's employee email accounts are for sale. Which action should the security team take FIRST?
Purchase the credential list to confirm authenticity before acting
Force password resets and revoke active sessions and tokens for the affected accounts
Publish a press release
Wait for evidence of fraudulent logins before responding
Invalidating exposed credentials quickly removes the attacker's immediate access. Waiting or buying the data from criminals delays containment and rewards the sellers.

A regional hospital wants to receive early warnings about ransomware campaigns targeting healthcare, and to exchange anonymized indicators with peer organizations. Which resource BEST supports this goal?
Internal SIEM dashboards only
Public vulnerability scanner
Unmoderated social media feeds
Sector-specific information sharing and analysis center
An ISAC lets members in the same sector share vetted threat information. Internal dashboards do not provide peer intelligence.
Which TWO are examples of open-source intelligence (OSINT)? (Choose TWO.)
Searching internet-exposed services and banners on Shodan
A paid vendor feed delivered under a non-disclosure agreement
Reviewing public WHOIS and DNS records for a suspicious domain
Correlated events from the company's own SIEM
A classified government threat bulletin
OSINT comes from publicly available sources such as internet search services and public registries. Commercial feeds, internal logs and classified bulletins are not open sources.

A company wants independent researchers to look for vulnerabilities in its production web application under published rules, paying only for validated findings. How does this approach BEST compare with a one-time penetration test?
It removes the need for a defined scope
It guarantees that all vulnerabilities will be found
It prevents any public disclosure of findings
It provides continuous, crowd-sourced testing with payment tied to valid results
A bug bounty program offers ongoing coverage from many researchers with diverse skills, paid by result. It still needs a scope and rules, and no method can guarantee that all flaws are found.
A SOC implements security orchestration, automation and response (SOAR). Which TWO benefits are MOST likely? (Choose TWO.)
Faster, more consistent response to common alerts
Reduced repetitive work for analysts
Elimination of the need for human oversight
Guaranteed absence of false positives
Removal of the need to test playbooks
SOAR speeds and standardizes routine tasks and frees analysts for complex work. It does not remove oversight, false positives or the need to test playbooks.
A SOAR playbook automatically blocks any IP address that appears in a newly subscribed, unvetted threat feed. Which risk is MOST significant with this configuration?
The feed will be encrypted
Analysts will have too little to do
Log retention will fall to zero
Legitimate business traffic may be blocked because of false positives, causing an outage
Automated blocking driven by an untested feed can disrupt valid partners or cloud services. The risk is mitigated by vetting feeds, adding approval gates and starting in alert-only mode.

Six months after deployment, an audit shows that many servers no longer match their approved security baseline because administrators made manual changes. Which approach BEST detects and corrects this drift on an ongoing basis?
Disabling local administrator accounts on workstations only
Automated configuration management with compliance scanning against the baseline
Rewriting the baseline document each quarter
Annual employee awareness training
Automated configuration management continuously compares systems with the baseline and can remediate deviations. Documentation changes do not alter system state.

Executives require that classified design files not be copied to removable media from company laptops, including when employees work from home on an untrusted network. Which control BEST enforces this?
Endpoint DLP agent with device control
Email gateway spam filter
Network DLP appliance at the data center edge
Web application firewall
An endpoint DLP agent enforces policy on the device itself, wherever it is connected. A network appliance only sees traffic that passes through it.
A newly deployed DLP system in blocking mode is rejecting a large number of legitimate emails and disrupting business. What is the BEST approach to resolve this while keeping the program on track?
Switch affected policies to monitor-only mode, tune rules using the results, then re-enable blocking in phases
Disable DLP permanently
Delete all existing policies and start with no rules
Allow all users to override every block without logging
Monitoring first and tuning reduces false positives before enforcement is turned back on. Disabling the system or removing logging eliminates the protection and the evidence.
A DLP team must detect leakage of the actual entries stored in a customer database, rather than any text that merely looks like a customer record. Which technique BEST accomplishes this?
Exact data matching or fingerprinting of the database
Keyword list of common surnames
Generic regular expression for names
Blocking all file transfers
Exact data matching compares content with hashes of real values and gives low false-positive rates. Generic patterns and keywords flag a lot of unrelated text.
Legal counsel informs IT that the company expects to be sued over a contract dispute. Mailbox retention currently deletes messages after 90 days. Which action should IT take FIRST?
Wait for a court order before preserving anything
Issue a legal hold and suspend automatic deletion for relevant custodians and systems
Export all mailboxes to personal devices
Delete irrelevant mailboxes to save storage
A legal hold preserves potentially relevant data once litigation is reasonably anticipated. Waiting risks spoliation of evidence.
A forensic examiner must acquire an image of a suspect's hard drive and be able to show in court that the original evidence was not modified. Which tool BEST helps?
Defragmentation utility
Hardware write blocker
Registry editor
Disk cleanup tool
A write blocker allows reading from the drive while preventing any writes. The other tools alter data on the drive.

Analysts suspect a server is sending large volumes of data to an external address. They need to see who talked to whom, how much and when, without inspecting payloads. Which data source is MOST useful?
NetFlow or IPFIX records
Email headers
Vulnerability scan results
Full disk image of the server
Flow records summarize conversations, with endpoints, ports and byte counts, and are lightweight. A disk image would not show network traffic metadata.
A SOC receives thousands of alerts per day, and most are closed as benign. Analysts are missing real incidents because of alert fatigue. Which action is BEST?
Hire a second shift and keep rules unchanged
Turn off alerting for low-priority sources entirely
Delay triage until the end of the week
Tune detection rules and thresholds, and suppress known benign patterns
Tuning reduces noise while keeping detection coverage. Disabling sources or delaying triage increases the chance of missing attacks.

A mobile app must sign users in with an external identity provider and receive basic profile information about the authenticated user. Which protocol is built on OAuth 2.0 specifically to provide this authentication layer?
RADIUS
Kerberos
OpenID Connect
LDAP simple bind
OpenID Connect adds identity tokens to OAuth 2.0 so that applications can verify who the user is. OAuth 2.0 alone is an authorization framework.
Several administrators share a single domain administrator password that has not changed in two years. Which solution BEST reduces the risk?
Posting the password in a restricted wiki
Requiring the password to be 6 characters longer
Emailing the password to new administrators
Privileged access management vault with credential check-out and automatic rotation
A PAM vault provides individual accountability, controlled check-out and rotation. Longer shared passwords still lack accountability.

A mail administrator wants receiving servers to verify that messages claiming to come from the company domain are legitimate, using both an authorized sending-server list and a cryptographic signature, with DMARC tying them to the visible From domain. Which TWO mechanisms does DMARC rely on? (Choose TWO.)
S/MIME
SPF
TLS 1.3
DKIM
PGP

DMARC evaluates SPF, which lists authorized sending servers, and DKIM, which signs messages, and checks alignment with the From domain. S/MIME and PGP are end-to-end message security and TLS only protects transport.
A tester has no access to source code but sends crafted inputs to a running staging web application to find injection and authentication flaws. Which testing method is this?
Code review
Dynamic application security testing
Static application security testing
Software composition analysis
Dynamic testing examines a running application from the outside. Static testing analyzes source code or binaries without executing them.
When a critical library vulnerability is announced, the company needs to quickly find out which of its applications include that library and its versions. Which artifact BEST supports this?
Software bill of materials
Service level agreement
Data flow diagram of the network
Business impact analysis
A software bill of materials lists the components within each application, which allows fast identification of affected software. The other documents do not list library components.

A company allows employees to read corporate email on personal phones. It wants to keep corporate data separated from personal content and be able to remove only the corporate data if the employee leaves. Which mobile control BEST achieves this?
Jailbreaking the device
Containerization through mobile device management
SMS-based notifications
Full device wipe for every user
Containerization creates a managed workspace that can be wiped selectively. A full wipe would remove the employee's personal data and may be inappropriate for BYOD.
A company wants Wi-Fi authentication that uses both server and client certificates for mutual authentication, with no passwords sent. Which EAP method is required?
PEAP with MS-CHAPv2
LEAP
EAP-MD5
EAP-TLS
EAP-TLS uses certificates on both the server and client sides. PEAP typically uses a server certificate with user credentials inside the tunnel.
An employee moved from finance to marketing two years ago, and the employee still has access to the general ledger. Which control BEST detects and corrects this privilege creep?
Longer passwords
Stronger firewall rules
Periodic user access reviews and recertification
Quarterly penetration tests
Periodic access reviews check whether permissions still fit the user's current role. The other controls do not compare access with job function.

A hunt team has no alert to follow. It starts from a hypothesis that an attacker is abusing built-in administrative tools to move laterally, and searches endpoint and authentication telemetry for supporting evidence. Which activity is this?
Threat hunting
Penetration test reporting
Vulnerability scanning
Tabletop exercise
Threat hunting is a proactive, hypothesis-driven search through telemetry for undetected threats. It is not triggered by an existing alert.

A system valued at $250,000 has an exposure factor of 30% for a given event, which is expected once every two years. A control costing $20,000 per year would reduce the annual rate of occurrence to once every ten years. What is the net annual benefit of the control?
SLE is $75,000. ALE falls from $37,500 to $7,500, saving $30,000, and subtracting the $20,000 cost leaves $10,000 net.
A risk team ranks risks as high, medium or low in workshops, using the judgment of business leaders, because reliable loss figures are not available. Which type of analysis is this?
Qualitative
Quantitative
Return on investment
Simulation of annual loss expectancy
Qualitative analysis uses categories and expert judgment. Quantitative analysis uses numeric values such as SLE and ALE.
A vendor offers a SOC 2 Type I report in response to a due diligence questionnaire. What is the main limitation of relying on this report?
It covers only physical controls
It contains no information about security
It is valid only for the vendor's own customers
It reports only on the design of controls at a point in time and not their operating effectiveness
Type I assesses control design on a single date, whereas Type II tests operating effectiveness over a period. Type II gives stronger assurance.

Two government agencies agree to cooperate on sharing threat information and record their general intentions, but the document is not legally binding and sets no specific performance obligations. Which document type is this?
Memorandum of understanding
Master services agreement
Business partners agreement with penalties
Service level agreement
An MOU expresses mutual intent and is generally non-binding. An SLA and an MSA define enforceable service terms.

A data controller discovers a breach of personal data of EU residents that is likely to create a risk to individuals. Under GDPR, within what time frame must the supervisory authority generally be notified?
72 hours
24 hours
7 days
30 days
GDPR requires notification without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours of becoming aware of the breach.
A policy document states: all company laptops must use AES-256 full disk encryption. Which type of governance document is this?
Guideline
Charter
Procedure
Standard
A standard defines mandatory, specific requirements. A procedure gives step-by-step instructions and a guideline is a recommendation.
Executives gather around a table and discuss how the company would respond to a ransomware scenario read out by a facilitator, with no systems touched. Which exercise is this?
Full interruption test
Failover test
Parallel processing test
Tabletop exercise
A tabletop exercise is a discussion-based walk-through of a scenario. It does not involve operational systems.

A red team and blue team work together during a test, sharing techniques and detection results in real time so the defenders can improve their controls immediately. What is this collaborative approach called?
Purple teaming
Bug bounty
White teaming
Black-box testing
Purple teaming combines offensive and defensive efforts to speed up learning. A bug bounty is a crowd-sourced program, not a joint internal exercise.
During a penetration test, the tester finds that an in-scope application is hosted on a third-party SaaS platform. What should the tester do BEFORE testing it?
Confirm written permission and review the provider's testing policy
Skip documentation of the finding
Use denial-of-service tools to test resiliency
Proceed because the customer owns the data
The provider owns the infrastructure, so its permission or policy must be followed before testing. Customer authorization alone does not cover systems the customer does not control.
An accounting clerk can create new vendors in the system and also approve payments to them. Which control BEST reduces the risk of fraud in this process?
Separation of duties
Longer password length
Data masking
Full disk encryption
Separating creation and approval requires collusion for fraud. The other controls do not address conflicting responsibilities.
A vulnerability cannot be remediated and the residual risk is rated high. Who should formally approve accepting that risk?
The risk owner or business executive accountable for the affected asset
The vulnerability scanner administrator
The help desk lead
The external auditor
Risk acceptance is a business decision made by the accountable owner or senior management. Auditors assess and do not accept risk on behalf of the organization.
A marketing app collects customers' dates of birth, home addresses and phone numbers, though it needs only an email address to send newsletters. Which privacy principle is being violated?
Data minimization
Data masking
Data sovereignty
Data retention
Data minimization means collecting only what is needed. Retention concerns how long data is kept.
A publicly traded company must show that its internal controls over financial reporting are effective and that executives attest to the accuracy of the statements. Which regulation applies?
SOX
PCI DSS
FERPA
HIPAA
The Sarbanes-Oxley Act regulates financial reporting and internal controls for public companies. PCI DSS covers payment cards and HIPAA covers health data.
Before signing a contract with a cloud provider, the procurement and security teams review its financial stability, certifications, references and breach history. Which concept does this describe?
Due diligence
Right to audit
Due care
Continuous monitoring
Due diligence is the investigation performed before entering an agreement. Due care is acting responsibly to maintain protection afterward.

Leadership states that the online store may experience up to two hours of downtime per month without escalation to the board, but anything beyond that must be reported. Which risk management concept does this describe?
Residual risk
Risk transference
Risk tolerance
Risk avoidance
Risk tolerance is the acceptable variation around objectives. Risk appetite is the broader level of risk the organization will pursue.
Which TWO factors are external considerations that influence an organization's security governance? (Choose TWO.)
Regulatory requirements
Industry standards and norms
The company's internal risk appetite
The company's organizational structure
The executive team's budget cycle
Regulations and industry norms originate outside the organization. Risk appetite, structure and budget cycles are internal factors.
A customer sends a formal request asking the company to provide a copy of all personal data it holds about the customer. Which privacy right is being exercised?
Right to object to profiling
Right to be forgotten
Right of access
Data portability only for employees
The right of access lets individuals obtain a copy of their personal data. The right to be forgotten concerns erasure.
A SOC manager wants a metric that BEST shows how quickly the team notices intrusions after they begin. Which metric should be used?
Annualized rate of occurrence
Mean time between failures
Recovery point objective
Mean time to detect
Mean time to detect measures the time between the start of an incident and its detection. MTBF refers to reliability of components.
